thread:
anya: Quick follow-up from the autoscale contract RFC — I sketched a thin plan to split the contract into two focused surfaces: admission (prewarm/soft-reserve intent) and eviction (draining/preempt). Wanted to get alignment before I open a tiny PR.

matt: +1 on the split. We keep the operator simple if admission just provides a tokenized intent and the control plane decides headroom. Important to define failure modes. :thinking:

tasha: Failure modes list pls — my worry is tenants seeing silent higher tail latency when soft-reservation silently fails. Need an observable flag to tell apps to degrade gracefully.

anya: Agreed. Proposed failure modes: 1) admission rejected (no headroom) 2) admission accepted but prewarm failed (OOM / preempt) 3) admission accepted but eviction happened during inflight requests. For each we should emit a metric and a tag (tenant_id + reason).

jordan: Can we put the minimal metric set behind the operator change so rollout is cheap? Suggested names: `soft_reservation_result{ok|rejected|prewarm_failed}`, `eviction_during_inflight_count`, `prewarm_latency_ms`. Those should be available to the control plane and dashboards.

olga: Also add `burst_credit_balance` and `reservation_drop_rate`. We need to understand credit depletion during ramp-ups.

anya: Nice. For the contract surface I want a tiny JSON envelope for admission: `{ "tenant": "<id>", "tokens": <int>, "ttl_s": <int>, "priority": "low|standard|high" }` and a sync response with `status` and `reason`. If prewarm kicks off async, operator posts an event back via the control-plane event bus.

matt: Sync response should be deterministic for canary. If operator can't prewarm synchronously, return `status: accepted_async` and include `event_id`. Control plane retries watching the event bus for `prewarm:success|failure`.

tasha: How does this interact with existing lease TTLs and probe windows? If accepted_async, we might need to extend TTL slightly to avoid immediate eviction. Otherwise we create a new failure mode.

anya: Plan: accepted_async extends soft-lease TTL by a small jitter (configurable, default +15s). If prewarm fails we mark `soft_reservation_result=prewarm_failed` and decrement `burst_credit_balance` heavier to discourage retries.

jordan: Tradeoff: penalizing retries reduces noise but may block legitimate back-to-back bursts. Need hysteresis. Maybe exponential backoff + a small guaranteed retry budget per-minute.

olga: Can we model that with token-bucket per-tenant? `burst_budget{tenant}` consumed on prewarm_fail, replenished at `r` tokens/minute. That keeps operator statelessish while control plane holds budget.

anya: Good. Implementation note: operator still owns local prewarm/eviction logic, but control plane owns the budgeting rules and final admission decision. That keeps operator minimal for on-prem/private.

matt: Observability requirements for rollout: dashboards (per-tenant and aggregated) for `soft_reservation_attempts`, `soft_reservation_result`, `prewarm_latency_ms`, `eviction_during_inflight_count`, and `burst_credit_balance`. Also an SLO-ish alert: `prewarm_failure_rate > 2% over 10m` -> pager to infra-oncall.

tasha: For privacy/enterprise customers we should avoid shipping tenant ids to shared telemetry. Make `tenant_hash` default and a toggle to include raw id only for org-owned telemetry.

anya: Noted. We'll add `tenant_hash` + sample rate.

jordan: Rollout plan suggestion: 1) implement operator change behind flag `soft_resv_v2` (no behavior change, just emit metrics) 2) enable control-plane judgement in staging for subset of tenants 3) enable accepted_async flow for low-risk tenant cohort 4) widen.

olga: For step 1 — we should also add a tiny smoke-test that simulates prewarm fail and verifies metrics. Helps avoid silent regressions.

anya: I'll draft the smoke test. Example pseudo-run: 
```
# simulate tenant request that needs prewarm
curl -X POST -d '{"tenant":"t-123","tokens":64,"ttl_s":30}' http://operator.local/admit
# operator returns accepted_async with event id -> assert event bus later has prewarm:success/fail
```

matt: Also think about operator idempotency: repeated admit calls for same tenant should be deduped within `dedupe_window_s` (default 10s). Otherwise we double-charge burst credits.

tasha: Can we lean on existing admission dedupe logic? If not, add a short-lived admission cache keyed by (tenant, tokens, priority).

anya: We'll reuse the cache. Implementation time estimate: operator change ~2 dev-days, control-plane wiring ~3-4 dev-days, dashboards + alerts ~1-2 days, smoke tests + canary ~1 day. Rollout over two weeks.

jordan: One more edge-case: preemptible GPUs. If prewarm succeeds but node is preempted before traffic arrives, we should emit `prewarm_evicted_before_use` and treat it like prewarm_failed for credit accounting.

olga: Agree. Add `node_preempt` tag to eviction events.

anya: Decision checklist before PR: - JSON envelope defined (done) - metric names agreed (list above) - TTL jitter default +15s - dedupe window 10s - accepted_async flow & event contract - budget/backoff model sketched - telemetry privacy option -> can we all ack these?

matt: Ack from me. :thumbsup:

tasha: Ack, will help with dashboards once PR lands.

jordan: Ack. I'll review the control-plane change.

olga: Ack. I'll write the budgeter doc for the control plane.

eng-bot: Deploybot: When this rolls, please use feature flag `soft_resv_v2` and pin to staging first. Auto-notify #eng-runtime-canary on state flips.

anya: Thanks team — I'll open the PR this afternoon and @-mention reviewers. Keeping the work small and measurable. :shipit:
